hook.line: This 19-year-old can make anything go viral.
hook.visual: Split screen: creator in a red-lit room on top, photos of the subject below swapping almost every word (plaque, car, chef costume), then her own clip.

beats.what: Top/bottom split: creator speaking over a photo of the subject; four cuts in the first 2.5 s swap the bottom photo.
Full-screen clip of the subject herself saying she can make anything viral (social proof in her own voice).
Zoom punch on the subject with a big red arrow pointing up at her as her name is said.
YouTube channel card with '5.53M subscribers' slides in over the creator as proof.
Promise: three things she does that you can steal.
Tip 1 (set expectations) shown with her pizza-challenge clip in a rounded card on a white background.
Tip 2 (foreshadowing and FOMO), explained back on the creator's face.
Tip 3: end the video right after the payoff.
Example clip in a rounded card: the subject at a drive-through asking what a dollar buys.
Creator ends abruptly on 'they won't click away just like this', using the tip on his own video.

why_it_works: Borrowed authority: a known creator's clips and subscriber count prove the claim before any advice is given.
Numbered list promise at 21 s ('three things you can steal') tells the viewer how long to stay.
Each tip is followed immediately by the subject's own clip, so the claim and the evidence arrive together.
The video ends on its own third tip, cutting right after the payoff, which pushes the loop back to the hook (loop 0.811).
weaknesses: 69 s with an 11.7 s longest shot of the creator talking; the middle stretch sags compared with the fast first 3 s.
Tip 2 is explained in words with little on screen to show it.
No ask at the end, so the 3.3M plays convert to few follows or comments (727).
for_robert: Copy the meta ending: have Fred deliver the last tip and the video cut off mid-reaction right after the payoff, so the reel proves its own advice and loops.
